comment: The distinction between authoritative deterministic services and model inference is valuable but currently presented as an emerging AI pattern rather than an architecture-wide safety principle. Exact, governed rules and probabilistic inference have different assurance needs and should not be blended invisibly.

public.text: The distinction between authoritative deterministic services and model inference is valuable but currently presented as an emerging AI pattern rather than an architecture-wide safety principle. Exact, governed rules and probabilistic inference have different assurance needs and should not be blended invisibly.
public.suggestedRevision: Elevate the principle, where a health-system function has an authoritative, exact or rule-bound answer- such as identity status, consent, units, eligibility, indicator definitions, reference calculations or authorisation- AI should invoke a governed deterministic service rather than recreate the result through inference. Reserve probabilistic methods for genuine uncertainty, preserve uncertainty explicitly, and keep inferred outputs distinguishable from authoritative facts and rules.
